name: SHOPLINE
tagline: Hosted e-commerce platform for online stores, with POS, payments, logistics and social selling channels bolted on, popular across Asia.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Plans vary by region and are often quoted per store with transaction fees on top.

verdictSummary: You can absolutely one-shot a storefront: product list, cart, Stripe Checkout, order table. What you cannot one-shot is the part people actually buy, which is being a merchant of record adjacent platform that already speaks to local payment methods, courier APIs, tax rules, POS hardware and Facebook / Instagram / LINE selling in half a dozen markets. Add PCI scope, chargebacks, fraud screening, refunds, inventory sync across channels, and a support line for when checkout breaks at 2am during a flash sale. A personal replacement makes sense only if you are one seller with a handful of SKUs and one payment provider. If you have real order volume, the DIY build is a liability, not a saving.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted single-vendor storefront with products, cart, Stripe Checkout, and an admin page listing paid orders.
requirements: Stripe account and API keys in .env
A host with a public HTTPS URL for webhooks
Your own answer for tax, invoicing and shipping labels
whatYouLose: Local payment methods beyond cards: bank transfer, e-wallets, convenience store pickup, installments
Courier and fulfilment integrations, shipping labels, tracking updates to buyers
POS, barcode scanning and offline / online inventory as one number
Social channel selling and catalog sync to Instagram, Facebook, LINE
Fraud screening, chargeback handling, PCI scope handled by someone else, and a support team when checkout dies mid-sale
moatNotes: Regional payments and logistics plumbing is boring, unglamorous, and takes years of contracts to assemble. That is exactly why it holds.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a storefront is the cheap part. Merchants pay for the fact that a customer in Taipei can pay by convenience store code, the parcel gets a label with a real tracking number, the inventory count matches the physical shop's POS, and none of that is the merchant's engineering problem. Uptime during a promotion is worth more than any feature, and a self-hosted Next.js store with one Stripe key does not offer that. The subscription is really rented operations.
notes: The storefront is a weekend; the store is not. The moat is regional payment rails, courier integrations and POS sync that took years of contracts to assemble.
prompt:
Build a single-vendor self-hosted storefront I can run for a tiny product catalog.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router, TypeScript) with Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/store.db
- Stripe Checkout for payment, Stripe webhook for order confirmation
- No user accounts, no CMS, no analytics, no telemetry

Data model:
- products: id, slug, title, description (markdown), price_cents, currency, stock, image_path, active
- orders: id, stripe_session_id, email, total_cents, currency, status, created_at
- order_items: id, order_id, product_id, title_snapshot, unit_price_cents, qty

Storefront:
- / lists active products with image, title, price
- /p/[slug] product page with quantity picker and add to cart
- Cart in a cookie, server-side price lookup only, never trust client prices
- /cart shows lines and a Checkout button that creates a Stripe Checkout Session server-side and redirects
- /success reads the session id and shows the order summary

Webhook:
- POST /api/stripe/webhook verifies the signature, handles checkout.session.completed, writes the order and items, decrements stock in one SQLite transaction, idempotent on stripe_session_id

Admin:
- /admin behind a single password from ADMIN_PASSWORD, HTTP basic is fine
- Table of orders with items and status, plus a form to create and edit products and upload one image each to ./public/uploads

Secrets in .env: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, ADMIN_PASSWORD, NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL. Include a .env.example.

Explicitly out of scope, do not build: discounts, multi-currency, tax calculation, shipping rates, courier labels, refunds, POS, multi-channel sync, email receipts beyond Stripe's own.

Ship a README with setup, `stripe listen` instructions for local webhook testing, and a seed script with three fake products.
